added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkeys, 1-week topical omidenepag isopropyl alone or with FP agonists, laser flare meter (report 104Fq080)

safety.confidence_note: Opening entry at the report date; the report itself is unpublished and known only from the FDA review.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkeys, 1-week topical omidenepag isopropyl alone or with FP agonists, laser flare meter (report 104Fq080)
safety.note: Non-GLP monkey study run in 2019 to probe ocular inflammation already seen in clinical study 33-001; public only in the 2022 FDA review.

safety.magnitude_basis: aqueous flare (photon counts/ms) on monotherapy D4/D7 vs D1 and combination vs monotherapy
safety.confidence_note: Reviewer summary of an unpublished non-GLP report; the quote is 40 words verbatim from the PharmR text bundle.
safety.judgement: Scored retro, not same: the FDA reviewer states the study was prompted by the clinical observation; patient side is study 33-001 and Omlonti label 5.3.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkeys, 1-week topical omidenepag isopropyl alone or with FP agonists, laser flare meter (report 104Fq080)
safety.note: Run after combination-arm inflammation in study 33-001; monkeys reproduced rising flare on monotherapy and more with FP agonists. Label 5.3 lists ocular inflammation.
safety.quote: The rationale for this study was the clinical observation (in clinical study # 33-001) that the combination of omidenepag isopropyl (0.003 to 0.03%) in combination with tafluoprost ophthalmic solution 0.0015% caused greater ocular inflammation than the omidenepag isopropyl monotherapy group.
safety.reason: Built to reproduce a known signal

added_models.model: C57BL/6J mice, omidenepag isopropyl 0.003% on the upper eyelid for 14 days vs bimatoprost (report 104Fm090)

safety.confidence_note: Opening entry at the FDA-listed report date (26 Jul 2019); paper epub 17 May 2020; abstract read.
safety.model: C57BL/6J mice, omidenepag isopropyl 0.003% on the upper eyelid for 14 days vs bimatoprost (report 104Fm090)
safety.note: Mouse eyelash study (report July 2019) predicted no prostaglandin-type eyelash growth; Japanese trials had already been read out.
safety.quote: Unlike existing prostaglandin analogs, our findings indicate that OMDI has no effect on eyelash growth in mice, suggesting that it may be a promising antiglaucoma agent with a reduced number of adverse effects.

safety.magnitude_basis: incidence of eyelash growth AE, omidenepag vs timolol/latanoprost, 3-month masked periods
safety.confidence_note: Paired by us (FDA statistical review table row, whitespace collapsed) with the mouse paper; columns are 011709IN, 011710IN, AYAME (DE-117, comparator) then pooled.
safety.judgement: Retro: the mouse study was run in 2019 after the Japanese phase 3 trials and 2018 Japanese approval, though before SPECTRUM 3/4 read out. Label 5.2 still carries a class eyelash-change warning.
safety.model: C57BL/6J mice, omidenepag isopropyl 0.003% on the upper eyelid for 14 days vs bimatoprost (report 104Fm090)
safety.note: Pooled phase 3: eyelash growth 0.7% on omidenepag vs 1.9% on timolol and 0.0% vs 0.5% latanoprost; no excess, as the mice showed.
safety.short: No eyelash growth excess in trials
safety.reason: Run after Japanese trials read out

added_models.model: Mouse 3T3-L1 preadipocyte differentiation (Oil Red O, Pparg/Cebpa) with omidenepag vs FP agonists (report 603Qn020)

safety.confidence_note: Proxy first-use year 2019 (filed to NDA; paper received 2019, epub 14 Jan 2020); abstract read.
safety.model: Mouse 3T3-L1 preadipocyte differentiation (Oil Red O, Pparg/Cebpa) with omidenepag vs FP agonists (report 603Qn020)
safety.note: Adipogenesis assay predicted omidenepag would not cause FP-agonist orbital fat atrophy (deepening of the upper eyelid sulcus).
safety.quote: Conclusions: A selective EP2 receptor agonist, OMD, did not affect the adipocyte differentiation in 3T3-L1 cells, whereas FP agonists significantly inhibited this process.

safety.magnitude_basis: PAPS signs (DUES) after switching from FP agonists to omidenepag
safety.confidence_note: Paired by us; small uncontrolled series, abstract only; the patient study began Nov 2018, before the assay was public.
safety.judgement: Absence-of-harm prediction scored same on uncontrolled switch series (n=11); Sakata 2021 (n=23, doi 10.1007/s10384-021-00855-3) found DUES improved in 16 eyes, none worse.
safety.model: Mouse 3T3-L1 preadipocyte differentiation (Oil Red O, Pparg/Cebpa) with omidenepag vs FP agonists (report 603Qn020)
safety.note: Prospective switch series: deepened upper eyelid sulcus improved, none worsened on omidenepag, consistent with no FP-type fat atrophy.
safety.short: DUES not caused; improved on switch
safety.quote: Some PAPS signs improved after patients started taking omidenepag isopropyl.

added_models.model: Human orbital fibroblast 3D organoids during adipogenesis, omidenepag vs bimatoprost acid

safety.model: Human orbital fibroblast 3D organoids during adipogenesis, omidenepag vs bimatoprost acid
safety.note: Academic HOF organoid study published after PAPS switch series were reported.
safety.quote: TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: The current study suggests that OMD may not induce deepening of upper eyelid sulcus (DUES).

safety.confidence_note: Abstract only; the organoids showed reduced PPARG and lipid staining with omidenepag, so the no-atrophy reading is the authors'.
safety.judgement: Retro: published April 2021 after the 2020 switch series; paired by us.
safety.model: Human orbital fibroblast 3D organoids during adipogenesis, omidenepag vs bimatoprost acid
safety.note: Organoids reproduced the no-DUES profile already reported in patients switched to omidenepag (Nakakura 2020, Oogi 2020).
safety.quote: Some PAPS signs improved after patients started taking omidenepag isopropyl.

added_models.model: ARPE-19, HRMEC and MG5 cells plus mouse intravitreal injection, omidenepag with latanoprost acid co-stimulation

safety.model: ARPE-19, HRMEC and MG5 cells plus mouse intravitreal injection, omidenepag with latanoprost acid co-stimulation
safety.note: Blood-retinal barrier model built after combination inflammation led to the FP-agonist combination warning.
safety.quote: In this study, we investigated effects of OMD and latanoprost acid (LTA), a FP agonist, on BRB and microglia in vitro and in vivo.

safety.magnitude_basis: inflammatory cytokines and outer BRB disruption with EP2+FP co-stimulation, none with either alone
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only; the patient side is stated, not cited to a trial, in the abstract.
safety.judgement: comparison_stated true: the paper sets its result beside the clinical combination restriction. Omidenepag alone was negative here, while the label lists monotherapy inflammation and CME; source_calls_it partial.
safety.model: ARPE-19, HRMEC and MG5 cells plus mouse intravitreal injection, omidenepag with latanoprost acid co-stimulation
safety.note: Co-stimulation, not omidenepag alone, raised IL-6/TNF and broke the outer BRB, reproducing the known combination inflammation.
safety.quote: Moreover, the combination use of the EP and the FP agonist is not recommended because of the risk of inflammation.

considered_not_added: Phase 1 healthy-volunteer IOP (Aihara 2019, PMID 31674861): a human datum for the draft's monkey track, not a model system
3T3-L1 3D organoids (Ida 2020, PMID 32994409): same assay system as the added 3t3l1-adipogenesis track; folded into it
Human trabecular meshwork / Schlemm's canal cell and 3D spheroid studies (PMIDs 34376747, 35067026, 36630412, 35329980, 34440134): mechanism only, no patient comparison
Rabbit and monkey ocular tissue distribution (PMID 39514219): PK only, no human ocular exposure comparison found
Normal and glaucomatous dogs and cats (PMIDs 42549739, 41332294, 41047758, 40714849): veterinary use after approval, never compared with human results
Excitotoxic retinal ganglion cell neuroprotection (PMID 38992567): no patient comparison (no neuroprotection trial)
Human conjunctival and corneal stroma fibroblast spheroids (PMIDs 37459581, 34914140): no patient comparison
Cystoid macular edema: case series only (PMIDs 40773215, 33692292, 37495978); no model of monotherapy CME found
Aganepag isopropyl and simenepag isopropyl: no admissible model source or patient comparison found (no FDA bundle, no PubMed hits)
No patient-level, PDX, human genetic or in-silico/QSP dose models exist for this class
